title: Immersed in microclimatic space: Microclimate experience and perception of spatial configurations in Dutch squares

findings.antecedent: Spatial configurations with some sense of enclosure (e.g., semi-enclosed places)
findings.mechanism: preference for spatial enclosure, smaller scale places and avoidance of large open space is consistent with findings from other studies (Carr et al., 1992; Gehl, 1987). Reasons for such preference were predom-inantly sought in 'proxemics'-the body of knowledge on spatial patterns based on people's social interaction and the minimum dis-tances related to those interactions (Gehl, 1987; Hall, 1966).

findings.mechanism: buildings described to be 'tall' in this case are at least 20 m high... areas around the feet of tall buildings are generally windy due to downwash effects
findings.quote: measurement data for two such places supported that these areas indeed had higher wind speeds than the areas considered comfortable in terms of wind

findings.mechanism: people often correctly read the cues for wind climate in these types of spaces.
findings.quote: Entrances of street canyons are perceived uncomfortably windy and can factually show strong wind effects.

findings.mechanism: street canyons can work as wind funnels increasing wind speeds due to higher pressure 'venturi' effects... angular building corners... more gusty
findings.quote: The street entrance areas clearly show higher wind speeds in our measurements than areas that are perceived comfortable in terms of wind.

findings.mechanism: people's interpretation of this spatial cue 'semi-enclosed area' has a high probability to be suitable.
findings.quote: Semi-enclosed areas are perceived to be 'comfortable in terms of wind' and this perception is often correct.

findings.mechanism: These areas can offer wind protection from three sides... a wake area is approximately 10-15 m
findings.quote: All the measurements taken in these areas showed indeed lower wind speeds than the ones taken in places considered to be 'windy'.

findings.mechanism: people's assessment might be based more on the reading of the spatial cues than the wind microclimate.
findings.quote: The foot areas of lower buildings are also perceived 'comfortable in terms of wind' but this depends on the building orientations.

findings.mechanism: downwash effects that are associated with taller buildings do not occur. Also the buildings provide wind protection for two directions
findings.quote: The averaged measurements taken in two typical spots also show lower wind speeds than the places perceived 'windy'.

findings.mechanism: People's perceptions do not seem to take this sufficiently into account in their judgments. It seems that in this case people's perception of 'comfort in terms of sun' is based more on the spatial setting than the real sun/shadow climate.
findings.quote: Semi-enclosed areas are often considered to be 'comfortable in terms of sun'-even if they are factually not that sun-exposed over the day.

stimuli.description: Three Dutch urban squares (Spuiplein in Den Haag, Neckerspoel in Eindhoven, Grote Markt in Groningen) where interviews and microclimate measurements were conducted.

limitations: Findings represent only a small fraction of possible relations that are expected to exist between spatial and microclimate perceptions.
Research was limited to specific sizes and spatial setups of squares in the Netherlands.
Future research should investigate different climate zones as people might develop different schemata and interpretations of spatial cues depending on regional climate.
